3110909.findings: Fan-shaped wall pocket vase with hanging hole, banded green/turquoise and orange-brown drip glaze typical of John Campbell Pottery, Launceston. Incised script signature on the back face near the hanging hole, partly obscured by glaze; reads as a looped 'J' / 'Campbell'-style script with 'Tas' trailing; not fully legible but consistent with Campbell incised marks. Tasmanian pottery with local collector market.
3110909.condition: No obvious chips or cracks visible; glaze pooling and small glaze bubbles/kiln grit on reverse are firing features. Lot tag tied through hanging hole.
3110909.reason: Signed John Campbell Tasmanian art pottery, large wall vase form, strong local collector demand.
3110909.marks_read: Incised script signature on reverse, partly obscured (likely John Campbell / Tasmania)

3110910.findings: Two pressed/moulded clear glass dog figures on frosted bases (a reclining dog with pup, a seated terrier). No maker's mark or label visible. Typical of French Cristal d'Arques / Verrerie souvenir pressed glass.
3110910.condition: Appear intact, no chips visible in photo.
3110910.reason: Common moulded French glass ornaments, low resale.

3110911.findings: Red cased ovoid studio glass vase. Base engraved 'ANDREW LAVERY 2000' (last digit possibly 9 but most likely 2000). Old gallery price sticker '$780' and stock sticker 'FL 104'. Signature supports the attribution. Andrew Lavery is an established Australian studio glass artist.
3110911.condition: Appears clean, no chips seen; stickers on base.
3110911.reason: Signed and dated Andrew Lavery studio glass with original $780 retail sticker; secondary market well below retail but collectable.

3110912.findings: Squat vase in brown/amber streaked glaze. Base hand-signed in slip 'W McHugh / Tasmania / 18' (dated 1918), William McHugh, Launceston (Tasmanian Potteries era). Early dated McHugh is sought after by Tasmanian pottery collectors. Signature supports the title.
3110912.condition: Crazing to base glaze, small brown glaze spot on base, light staining inside; no chips or cracks visible on rim or body.
3110912.reason: Signed and dated 1918 W McHugh Tasmanian pottery, large size, strong local collector market.

3110913.findings: Tall banquet-style kerosene lamp with pierced/cast brass font cover, twisted column and ornate cast foot, frosted pink-tinted moulded glass shade with gilt and etched paisley panels, clear chimney. Style of American Victorian 'Gone with the Wind' / banquet lamps c1890-1920. No maker's mark visible in photos (burner not shown closely).
3110913.condition: Brass with patina/oxidation; shade appears intact; burner wick knob present. Electrified status unknown.
3110913.reason: Decorative unmarked banquet lamp, moderate decorator value only.

3110914.findings: Black glazed plaster/chalkware TV lamp of a dancing island girl with drum and palm frond, light fitting at back. Title says 'Barsony style', i.e. not attributed to Barsony; base has no Barsony stamp or label visible.
3110914.condition: Wear and chips to black finish at base edges, bulb fitting rewired with modern cord.
3110914.reason: Unmarked Barsony-style retro lamp, not an attributed Barsony piece.

3110915.findings: Twisted ribbed red-to-amber/green sommerso art glass lamp base, Murano style, brass bayonet fitting. No label or signature visible.
3110915.reason: Unattributed Murano-style glass lamp base, modest value.

3110916.findings: Circular pastel or watercolour portrait miniature of a young woman with pearl earring, gilt slip in turned mahogany frame. Verso has partial blue and gilt trade label 'Doni ... / H.T. COSTANTINI / ...' (Costantini, likely Florence or Rome dealer/framer). Unsigned on visible front. Pleasing quality, plausibly 19th century.
3110916.condition: Backing taped with old black tape, label torn/partial, frame with minor knocks; image appears clean.
3110916.reason: Attractive 19th century portrait miniature with Italian dealer label, decent decorative market.

3110917.findings: Ribbed clear pressed glass ball match striker with oval panel moulded 'Schweppes DRY GINGER ALE' with orange paint infill.
3110917.condition: Paint infill mostly intact, some wear; no chips visible.

3110918.findings: Small cream jug in blue with yellow drip glaze, handle in amber/yellow. Base incised 'W McHugh / Tasmania' (no date visible). Supports title. William McHugh Tasmanian pottery.
3110918.condition: Blue glaze flecks on white rim, light staining inside base; no chips clearly visible.
3110918.reason: Signed W McHugh Tasmanian pottery, collectable locally.
